title: Streaming embeddings sampler rounding bias causing small undercount in usage
creator: Aditi Shah
description:
Summary:
Customers using streaming embeddings endpoints show a small but measurable undercount (~1-2%) compared to non-streaming/batch embeddings for equivalent workloads. This ticket tracks the triage, reproduction, root cause analysis, and remediation plan.

Background:
- We have two ingestion paths for embeddings: batch (synchronous per-request accounting) and streaming (chunked tokenization + sampler that emits partial token attributions to the aggregator).
- Around 2026-02-20 we started seeing a persistent ~1.1-1.9% divergence in billed tokens for a set of large customers using streaming embeddings heavily. The discrepancy is stable across time and workloads.

What we observed so far:
- Aggregated usage reports (daily) show streaming-backed embeddings routes are ~1.5% lower than expected given identical content fed through batch endpoints.
- Difference persists after normalizing for request size, embedding dims, and compression.
- Sampling code for streaming path uses per-chunk fractional counters (float32) and rounds down when merging into the per-key ledger. Batch path uses integer token counts and preserves exact per-request token_count metadata.
- In high-churn workloads (many small chunks), repeated floor rounding of 0.3-0.7 fractional tokens per chunk accumulates into measurable undercount.

Hypothesis / Root cause:
- The streaming sampler emits fractional token attributions per chunk into an in-memory float32 accumulator. When the accumulator flushes to the ledger it casts to int32 (floor) and the remainder fractional part is dropped. Because streaming produces many small partial attributions, the rounding bias drifts negative. The batch path does not suffer this because it uses whole-token accounting per request.
- Secondary factor: aggregator compaction runs with a lower precision summarization job that coalesces adjacent flushes and can drop <1 token fractions if a compaction window occurs before a later compensating attribution arrives.

Repro steps (local):
1) Generate a corpus of 50k short texts and call streaming embeddings with chunk_size=16 and streaming chunk flush=50ms.
2) Replay the same corpus via batch embeddings route.
3) Compare per-api-key daily token totals after 24 hours. Expect ~1-2% lower totals on streaming path.
4) Instrumentation: enable METER_VERBOSE for test keys to capture per-chunk fractional_attribution values and flush events.

Data collected:
- Attachments: perf dump (s3://redwood-testing/emb-stream-bias/2026-03-05/dump-01.log)
- Representative counts: key=acct-77: batch_tokens=12,134,021 streaming_tokens=11,965,462 delta=1.4%
- Sample per-chunk fractions: many 0.36, 0.48, 0.29 values repeated thousands of times for that key.

Short-term mitigations:
- Increase streaming accumulator precision to float64 to reduce rounding noise (temporary patch deployed to staging; reduces bias by ~60%).
- Disable aggressive compaction for metering-aggregator for streaming keys (feature-flagged).

Long-term fix plan:
1) Change ledger commit contract: record fractional micro-tokens in fixed-point integer (microtokens) rather than float-per-chunk floor casting. This will guarantee conservation of token attributions when merging flushes.
2) Update aggregator compaction to preserve fractional microtokens and only round at final billing export boundary using bankers rounding.
3) Add deterministic unit+integration tests that simulate high-churn streaming and assert zero net drift vs batch path.
4) Backfill: run a reconciliation job to estimate lost microtokens for affected keys and emit corrective invoice line items / internal credit adjustments for impacted customers (requires billing & legal alignment).

Acceptance criteria:
- Streaming vs batch for synthetic workloads shows delta <= 0.01% after fixes and tests.
- No change to customer-visible latency or memory beyond acceptable ranges.
- Backfill plan approved by finance and ops.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Tolerance threshold for rounding on legacy invoices (finance needs a proposal).
- Whether to apply backfill credits for accounts with delta < 0.5% (cost/operational trade-off).
- Migration rollout order for Dedicated and Private instances (some customers run metering offline and require package upgrade).
